**Rule coverage.** G1 R1 (timestamps ≤ min(commit, clock) + 5 min; date-only ≤ max(commit UTC date, committer-local date)), R2 (acts ≥ commit − 48 h unless `≤`/`retro:`/`as-of` or a plain correction carrying the true date), R3, R5 (`future-ok: <class>: <reason>`, expiring allow entries), R6, malformed `x` stamps; positions = PHASE LOG lead dates, GATE DECISIONS bullets and date-headed table rows, `updatedAt`, BUILD_INDEX `landed`, DEFERRALS status dates, run/PR header stamps, readout stamps, plan-extension and `> Amended` dates, new-ADR `Date:`, landed-ADR status/trigger-evaluation dates, `*.jsonl` `recorded_at` (act) / `observed_at`, `assessed_at` (event), digest headings, policy `date` paths. Scope: `docs/build`, `docs/tickets`, `docs/adr` + policy paths; `docs/build/planning/**` and `docs/build/logs/**` excluded. **Blame mode:** a GATE DECISIONS table whose caption bullet says ``RESTORED from `<sha>^` `` — every row verbatim at `<sha>^`, dated against `git blame -w <sha>^`; a clock-false row needs an annotation row `| R<n> | … clock-false / DATE CORRECTION … |` after the block or a `date_corrections.csv` row naming `restored R<n>`; restored rows are not judged by diff mode. **G2 core:** every BM-HIST-01 region/file mode of the skill's history mode (ported), plus the landed-ADR rule from the orchestrator's note (only `## Status updates` at EOF or `### Trigger evaluation …` at the end of `## Revisit trigger`; a bare status line at EOF stays allowed for skill parity; every ADR id named must exist at the judged head). **G4a** (7-column tables): ISO-Z date, kind vocabulary (+ `date-correction`), verbatim quote or `provided: yes/no`, scoped pre-authorization, hedge → later plain `confirmation`, delegation, answer-after-pause (a chain marker without a pause fails; other gates warn); restored tables skipped; a delegation quoted in a legacy bullet is a warning. **G4b:** guard sentence on new readouts, append-only except one `Status:` line in the vocabulary, signing diffs add only Signature-block lines + agent-drafted blocks, decision words equal a GATE DECISIONS quote, drafted-block sha256, confirmation quoting the hash prefix and recorded as a `confirmation` row, no ticks.

**Agent interpretations (labelled; for the orchestrator to confirm or reverse).**
1. Exit 2 = usage *or* not applicable (B4 §3; the unit prompt); the skill's own script uses 5 for bad arguments — the hand-off only ever passes well-formed arguments, so the two agree in practice.
2. The marker check accepts the checkout's README (as `check-history.sh` reads it) or the judged revision's; the policy and guards marker come from the judged revision when it has them, else the checkout (so replays of pre-v2 commits run under today's policy, as the skill's replay does). A change can therefore amend its own policy — policy edits must be reviewed like code.
3. `allow` entries exempt only dates ≤ their expiry (stricter than the skill, which exempts any date on a matching line).
4. The `exempt` rule is written without the leading `###`: `check-history.sh` strips `␣#…` as a comment, which would leave an empty heading and silently exempt nothing under `--no-hook`. Upstream skill bug — see open issues.
5. BUILD_INDEX seq uniqueness applies only to index tables (a `PR` or `landed` column); a corrections table may name one seq per corrected field. Column count applies to every added row.
6. A run ledger is "closed" only by a dated `Closed:` stamp in its header (before the first `##`); `- **Closed:** none.` in a body section is neither a stamp nor a close (the `d7cbc68e` shape; the skill matches it anywhere).
7. No revisit-trigger hash is computed here (G8-3 is SEED-15's); if one is, hash only the text before the first `### Trigger evaluation` (orchestrator note).

## Open issues / hand-offs

1. **SEED-02b (context 2):** `make docs-check-memory/-spec/-matrix`, the memory-guard step in the CI `docs` job (needs `fetch-depth: 0`, which the job has), pytest collection of `docs/build/tools/test_*.py` (the oracle tests skip on the `python` job's shallow checkout; the synthetic tests need only `git`), and `ci_boundary.py` (reuse `memory_guard.read_ci_required()`).
2. **SEED-02c (context 3):** the OM-01 trailer grammar is not in this guard; the vendored `check-history.sh` it is adding delegates to this file when present — no change needed for the hand-off.
3. **Upstream skill (B6 follow-up, not edited):** `check-history.sh` strips `␣#…` as a comment, so `exempt <path> ### <heading>` loses its heading (written here without `###`); its `date` rules make every match an act (no `act-when`); its allow entries exempt any date on the line; it treats `Closed` anywhere in a run ledger as closed. All matter only under `--no-hook` / `--replay`.
4. **Conventions the guard relies on (for SEED-08, SEED-09, SEED-10, T5):** the restored caption is the last bullet before its table; annotation rows start `| R<n> |`; the archived LEDGER head and the head replacement land in the **same commit**, with a pointer comment naming the archive file; DEFERRALS flips read `DONE <date -u> (evidence) — was: OPEN …`; a correction that quotes an old date says `DATE CORRECTION` or `recorded … → true …` with the true date (else R2); Round-11 GATE DECISIONS rows are ISO-Z, quoted, `kind`-typed, appended at the end of the 7-column table; a gate-marker `decision` needs a PHASE LOG pause entry naming the marker in the same round.
5. **Guards marker:** not in `docs/build/README.md` yet (T5) — until then the owed kind-P DEFERRALS rule-5 is a warning.
6. **Not in this context (owned elsewhere):** G2 full modes (`placeholder-fill`, `frozen-snapshot`, event-coupled `row-annotate`, jsonl schema/chaining) → M1/M6 (P34.7); G5 ledger contract → M2 (P34.9); G1 R4 and the whole-tree code-literal test → B1's tickets (P34.22); G4c operator signing key → operator decision; planning-ledger freshness (V14) → the vendored validator's `--planning` mode.
